title: Localized bounded internal-Hom comparison by finite tails
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a commutative ring, $t\in A$, and $R$ a sheaf of commutative $A$-algebras. Work in the derived category $D(R)$ of module sheaves and its scalar localization $Q_t:D(R)\to D(R)[1/t]$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P$ be a cochain complex with $P^r=0$ outside an integer interval $[a,b]$, and let $f:M\to N$ be any map of possibly unbounded complexes. Write $c_V=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(V,f)$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. Assume $Q_t(c_{P^r[0]})$ is an isomorphism for every $r\in[a,b]$. Then
$$Q_t(c_P):Q_t\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_t\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,N)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(R)[1/t]$. More precisely, put $P_{\ge r}=P$ in degrees at least $r$ and zero below. The three comparisons for $P^r[-r]$, $P_{\ge r}$ and $P_{\ge r+1}$ form a morphism of the distinguished triangles induced by the degreewise split sequence $0\to P_{\ge r+1}\to P_{\ge r}\to P^r[-r]\to0$, with all connecting squares commuting, before and after $Q_t$. Under the signed Hom source-shift isomorphisms, $c_{P^r[-r]}$ identifies with $c_{P^r[0]}[r]$, naturally in $f$. For a degree-zero source module the comparison from $\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P^r[0],M)[r]$ to $\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P^r[-r],M)$ multiplies a component in degree $q$ by $(-1)^{rq}$, and the same formula is used for $N$. The assertion includes $P=0$ and empty support intervals; it assumes neither that $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism nor that the terms of $P$ are projective.

source.place: Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), termwise split Hom sequences; agent-written finite localized comparison with signed shifts, old proof steps 7–9.

proof.text: For every integer $r$, write $T_r=P_{\ge r}$ and $G_r=P^r[-r]$. The inclusion $i_r:T_{r+1}\to T_r$ and projection $p_r:T_r\to G_r$ are chain maps: at the cut the only outgoing differential in $G_r$ is zero and the only incoming differential in $T_r$ is zero. In each degree their sequence is either $0\to P^j\xrightarrow{1}P^j\to0$ or $0\to0\to P^r\xrightarrow{1}P^r\to0$, or zero. Thus $0\to T_{r+1}\xrightarrow{i_r}T_r\xrightarrow{p_r}G_r\to0$ is degreewise split. Its degreewise splittings need not be chain maps.

source.place: Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), termwise split source sequence; explicit stupid-tail construction.

proof.text: For the canonical stupid-filtration source sequence of step 1, use its degreewise splittings and the proved generic splitting helper of [lem-pc-stupid-tail-hom-short-exact]. In each Hom degree use the product universal property [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections] to precompose with the degreewise splitting maps. The componentwise composition formula shows that these maps split the reversed Hom row. The additive precomposition formula gives the middle splitting identity. Hence the specified canonical Hom rows are short exact. Naturality of the Hom bifunctor [def-pur-hom-complex] in the target gives the two squares for postcomposition by f. This proves row_zero, row_shortExact and row_comm for the actual maps, not merely an isomorphic unspecified row.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), product and differential; Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), termwise split Hom observation.

proof.text: The category of sheaves of $R$-modules is abelian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the rows and their morphism in step 2. In $D(R)$ this gives distinguished triangles $H(G_r,V)\to H(T_r,V)\to H(T_{r+1},V)\xrightarrow{\delta_V}H(G_r,V)[1]$ and a morphism between them with the three comparisons as components. In particular its connecting square is the specified equality $c_{G_r}[1]\circ\delta_M=\delta_N\circ c_{T_{r+1}}$; this uses naturality of the canonical short-exact-sequence connecting map, rather than a choice of a filler for the first two squares.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), natural distinguished triangle of a short exact sequence.

proof.text: The structure map $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,R)$ gives the canonical $A$-linear structure on module sheaves and on $D(R)$ [def-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-coefficient-actions]; by [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category] the localization from complexes is $A$-linear and every shift of $D(R)$ is $A$-linear. By [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated], $D(R)[1/t]$ is triangulated and $Q_t$ is exact. Apply it to both triangles and the morphism of step 3. Functoriality preserves all three equalities, including $Q_t(c_{G_r})[1]\circ Q_t(\delta_M)=Q_t(\delta_N)\circ Q_t(c_{T_{r+1}})$. This proves the triangle assertion before and after localization.

source.place: Tag 05R6 (proposition-construct-localization), exact triangulated localization, applied to the scalar-localization theorem.

proof.text: Construct the normalized single-term shift directly from the projections [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections]. All factors except the source degree k are zero. Apply the already proved private helper CategoryTheory.fan_projection_isIso from the module of [lem-pc-single-degree-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso] to conclude that projection to that factor is an isomorphism; no local duplicate of that helper is needed. Composing it with the canonical identification of the single term gives singleProjection. Its differential is postcomposition by d_V, since the single source has zero differential, and its map formula is postcomposition by f. In degree q define the required isomorphism by projecting the degree-zero-source Hom shifted by r, multiplying by (-1)^(rq), and inverting the projection for the source in degree r. The identity (-1)^r(-1)^(r(q+1))=(-1)^(rq) proves the chain condition for every integer r and q. The component projection equality gives exactly the prescribed normalization. The map formula gives naturality in the target. Applying the exact functor from complexes to the scalar-localized derived category and its shift comparison transports termwise invertibility to the first term of each tail triangle.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), Hom differential and signed source-shift reindexing; specialization m=-r.

proof.text: First suppose $a\le b$. Prove by downward induction, for $r=b+1,b,\ldots,a$, that $Q_t(c_{T_r})$ is invertible. At $b+1$ the source complex is zero, so both Hom complexes are zero and the comparison is their identity. For $a\le r\le b$, the triangle morphism of step 4 has invertible first component by step 5 and invertible third component by the induction hypothesis. The two-isomorphisms criterion [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes its middle component $Q_t(c_{T_r})$ invertible. At $a$ we have $T_a=P$. If $a>b$, every term of $P$ is zero, so the conclusion follows immediately from the zero-source calculation; the same calculation handles $P=0$ with any interval. The construction of the triangle morphisms and signed squares was valid for every $r$, so it also supplies those assertions in these degenerate cases.

source.place: Tag 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle), finite downward induction along the triangles of steps 3–4.
